hw_centurion.text: Ave! I'm a Roman soldier, between jobs. The legions marched twenty miles a day in full kit, which is a pack, a spade, a stake and a very opinionated mule.
Soldiers on the Wall came from Spain, Syria, Belgium and the Danube. It was the most multicultural place in Britain, and they all complained about the weather.

hw_ranger.text: The Wall was painted white once, and plastered. In the sun it must have shone like a long, slightly smug chalk line across the country.
The stones you see were reused in later centuries for farm walls and churches. A good deal of Northumberland is Roman, with extra sheep.

hw_volunteer.text: Be gentle. Folk come here to stand. Some just sit. Everyone lowers their voice, without being asked.
They took cuttings and seeds, and the saplings are growing on, safe, in nurseries. A tree is slow, but it's good at beginnings.

hw_walker.text: Eighty-four miles of the Hadrian's Wall Path, coast to coast. The trail goes up, down, up, down, with a view at the top of every up and a sandwich at the bottom of every down.
My feet have opinions. I haven't been told them yet. They are saving them for the second day.

hw_shepherd.text: Sheep don't care about the Wall. They go over it, under it and through any gap they find. Hadrian planned for Picts. He did not plan for Swaledales.
I counted two hundred this morning. Then I counted two hundred and four. Then I gave up.
